knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A numeric matrix or data frame containing the raw, untransformed intensity data of a single microarray scanned at multiple (two or more) scanner settings. Rows represent individual spots/probes, and columns represent scans.
- alternatives: A web interface based on the original Fortran code (available at http://www.bioss.ac.uk/ktshowcase/create.cgi) which uses a different implementation of the Nelder-Mead simplex method.
- when_to_use: Use when you have multiple scans of the same microarray at different scanner sensitivity settings and want to combine them to obtain a single, optimal estimate of gene expression that minimizes signal censoring for highly expressed genes and noise for weakly expressed genes.
- pitfalls: Input data must be on the raw scale and NOT log-transformed or otherwise transformed. The algorithm is computationally slow and memory-intensive; for very large datasets, it is recommended to first fit the model on a random subset (e.g., 10,000 rows) to obtain initial values for scanning effects and scale parameters before fitting the full dataset.

workflows.name: estimate_gene_expression_multiscan
workflows.intent: Estimate gene expressions from multiple laser scans of a single microarray and perform model diagnostics.
input: intensity_data.csv (a CSV file containing raw, untransformed intensity measurements with rows as probes and columns as scans at different sensitivity settings)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the raw intensity data ;; 2. Fit the non-linear functional regression model using multiscan ;; 3. Inspect the fitted model object ;; 4. Extract the estimated gene expressions ;; 5. Plot the fitted model and diagnostic residuals
workflows.code:
data(murine)
fit<-multiscan(murine)
fit
str(fit)
gene.exprs<-fit$mu
plot(fit)
op<-par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(fit,residual=TRUE)
par(op)
